A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ER− breast cancer is a misnomer and that ER− breast cancers are not ER−.
ER+ breast cancer cells can be classified into two types on the basis of a functional assay of ER-ERE interaction.

ER+ breast cancer cells can be classified into three categories: (1) ER+, ERd+ (ERd+ breast cancer cells are sensitive to hormone therapy); (2) ER+, ERi+ (ERi+ breast cancer cells should be resistant to hormone therapy); and (3) ER− (ER− breast cancer cells are insensitive to hormone therapy).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ER assay should be based on the downstream functional assay for ER-ERE complex interaction and not only the initial ligand-binding assay.
ERi+ breast cancers are not responsive to anti-estrogen therapy.
ERi+ breast cancers should not be subjected to anti-hormonal therapy, and this will prevent unnecessary suffering for patients and also save money.
